messages.body_plain:
"Default values" are a feature of functions, so you can wrap a
function around knit_expand() to achieve this goal, e.g.

library(knitr)
f = function(x, y = 2, ...) {
  knit_expand(text = "x is {{if (missing(x)) 'unknown' else x}}, and
y+1 is {{y+1}}", ...)
}

> f()
[1] "x is unknown, and y+1 is 3"
> f(x = 'foo')
[1] "x is foo, and y+1 is 3"

I'm not sure if this answers your question.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Beamer to Markdown conversion?
messages.body_plain:
In theory, you can just use <<>>= for R Markdown. The knitr document
parser and renderer are independent, i.e. you can use the Rnw parser,
but with the Rmd renderer. For example,

library(knitr)
pat_rnw()
render_markdown()
out = knit(text = '<<foo,tidy=FALSE>>=
 1+1
@'
)
cat(out)

You will get Markdown output:

```r
 1+1
```

```
## [1] 2
```

This is probably not well-known to most knitr users, and I have rarely
mentioned it in the public. Although this is possible, I do not want
to have a mixture of syntax in mind, so you are still recommended to
make the conversion. Below is the code that I wrote in two minutes and
was not tested:

library(knitr)
x = readLines('foo.Rnw')
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$chunk.begin, '```{r \\1}', x)
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$chunk.end, '```', x)
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$inline.code, '`r \\1`', x)
writeLines(x, 'foo.Rmd')

Converting other LaTeX commands to Markdown should be easy with
Pandoc, but I guess the pain is that Rnw is not LaTeX, and I'm not
sure what Pandoc is going to do with the R code chunks when converting
the Rnw document to Markdown.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Separate your calculations from presentation. I usually put my input and processing steps into an R file. Then I create an R file where I setup any calculation parameters, source the calculations file, and use save.image() to store the results. Then I create the Rnw file that re-loads any needed libraries and uses the load() function to pull the results into memory, and the rest of the Rnw file renders the output. As I refine my calculations I move more and more of them into functions that produce objects and fewer global variables are used. I'm aware of the problem: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/607
This will require a change of the design, so it is unlikely to happen
very soon. For your specific case, my suggestion is to use a chunk
hook instead. Here is a quick example:

unlink('my_report.R')
opts_chunk$set(purl = TRUE)
knit_hooks$set(purl = function(before, options, envir) {
  if (before || !options$purl) return()
  # write code after a chunk
  cat(options$code, file = 'my_report.R', sep = '\n', append = TRUE)
})

I do not quite like the current design of purl(), since it is not
consistent with knit(). I'll think more about it in the future.
